params.body:
## What went wrong

On 2 October 2026 a HEIC photo uploaded from a computer failed in every converter with "Unsupported codec". The server had libheif, and Imagick listed HEIC and HEIF as formats, but the HEVC decoder was missing: on Ubuntu 24.04 libheif ships its codecs as separate plugin packages and only the AV1 ones were installed, not `libheif-plugin-libde265`.

`HeicConverter::available()` only asked whether a driver knows the FORMAT (`Imagick::queryFormats('HEI*')`), so the upload door let the file in, the conversion failed, and the dealer read "conversion failed, try again" instead of the refusal that says what to do. The smoke test asked the same question and printed "ok". It stayed hidden for weeks because an iPhone uploading from the phone itself hands over a JPEG; HEIC only arrives from desktops.

Fixes bevinding heic-formaat-gekend-maar-niet-te-decoderen.

## What changes

- **A real probe.** `HeicConverter::canDecode()` converts a 613-byte HEVC-coded sample that ships with the code (`resources/data/heic-sample.heic`, 64x64, brand `heic`, written with `sips`) and checks that a readable JPEG comes out. `probe()` returns the same answer with the driver that decoded or the reason none did.
- **`available()` now means "can really convert"**: a driver is present and it decoded the sample. `UploadedImage` is unchanged and so refuses a HEIC with the existing "set the camera to Most Compatible" message on a server without the decoder, before trying anything. The fall-through over the other drivers in `toJpeg()` is as it was (moved into a private `attempt()` that the probe shares).
- **Cached per release.** Key `heic.can_decode.<commit>` (from `BuildStamp`), so a deploy asks again. A yes holds for as long as the release runs; a no is asked again after ten minutes, so a decoder installed outside a deploy opens the door by itself. Within one process the decode runs at most once, and never on a request that carries no HEIC. A failed probe writes one warning to the log.
- **`stocklist:smoke heic`** decodes now (not from the cache) and writes the answer back, so the upload door follows it at once:
  - `✓ heic  HEIC wordt omgezet naar JPEG met imagick; decodeert een staal: ja`
  - `✗ heic  omzetter imagick kent het formaat; decodeert een staal: nee (imagick: ... Unsupported codec ...). ... Op Ubuntu is de HEVC-decoder een apart pakket: sudo apt-get install -y libheif-plugin-libde265, daarna PHP-FPM herladen en deze controle opnieuw draaien`
  - `– heic  geen HEIC-omzetter op deze machine; ...` when there is no driver at all (unchanged: a shortage, not a failure).

  A driver that is present but cannot decode is a failure with exit code 1 on every environment, the same convention as the other local-capability line (`showroom`); no driver at all stays a skip, as before.
- **Koppelingen and Werking** already show the `heic` line from the same check and the same cache, so they now show the failure too; no screen code changed.
- **`phpunit.xml` pins `HEIC_CONVERTER=none`**, so the rest of the suite (the `--all` smoke tests) gives the same heic line on a laptop, on the runner and anywhere else. The converter tests set the driver themselves.
- README (server requirements) and CLAUDE.md (Gotchas): HEIC needs libheif with the libde265 plugin, check with `php artisan stocklist:smoke heic`.

## Rules

- New `R S1-6.42`: HEIC at the upload door, and what "the server can" means.
- New `R P3-13.10`: what the heic line of the smoke test measures and when it fails.
- Finding `2026-10-02-heic-formaat-gekend-maar-niet-te-decoderen`, resolved.

## Tests

`HeicDecodeProbeTest` scripts the driver layer (which drivers know the format, what a conversion does), so it does not depend on the machine: the probe is false when the driver throws "Unsupported codec" or writes something that is not a JPEG, true when it writes one; the answer is cached per release and a no expires after ten minutes; the upload door refuses with `photos.heic_unsupported` without touching the upload; the smoke line in all three states, and that it measures fresh. The sample's brand is recognised by `looksLikeHeic`. One test runs the real conversion on the machine's own drivers and skips with what it found when the machine cannot decode, so the CI log states what the runner has.
params.title: HEIC is probed by decoding a sample: a server without the HEVC decoder refuses clearly and the smoke test says so
